note: The `<OptionCards>` entry's own specimen: three tool-breaking modes, one of them disabled with a stated reason rather than dimmed silently. It renders through `<Field as="fieldset">`, which is the single shipped fieldset host in the corpus, so a `disabled` group here is also the proof that a fieldset disables every descendant control. THE `legend` KNOB DRAWS NOTHING and that is correct: `.manager-resolution-mode-legend` is `position: absolute` at 1x1px in the global sheet, so the legend is the group's ACCESSIBLE name and never a visible heading. context.why: The Difficulty card of the Checks studio. Six plain scalars, and every prop the primitive receives is then computed by the card itself — `selectedValue={resolvedDcMode}` is a `$derived` of `dcMode`, which is the kind of expression no static extractor can resolve. `showDcSource` is `true` because the chooser renders only on the SIMPLE slot, where the model carries `dcMode`.

context.why: The COMPARISON control on the Difficulty card — meet-or-exceed against exceed — which is a two-segment track beside a `Stepper` and a `RadioCardGroup`. note: `as` opens on `div` rather than on the majority `label` host for one reason: the `field` filler is itself a `<Field as="label">`, and a label inside a label is invalid HTML with an ambiguous click target. The host story pins `children` to plain text so all three hosts stay valid.

states.hover: No prop, and none is wanted: the field is a column, not a control, and what hovers inside it is the caller's own input.
states.focus-visible: No prop. The ring belongs to whatever control the field wraps; tab into the specimen on the plinth to see it.
states.loading: No prop. A field shell renders whatever it is handed, synchronously.
states.invalid: No prop. `library.html:646` specifies `invalid` and `error` on the 38px control shell, and that shell is NOT built — only this column is — so there is nowhere for an error line to be rendered and nothing to mark.
states.readonly: No prop, for the same reason: `readonly` belongs to the unbuilt control, and a `readonly` attribute passed through the rest spread would land on a `<div>` and do nothing.
states.empty: Not applicable: a field is a shell around a caller's control, so it holds no collection that could be empty. Clearing `children` renders an empty box, which is a missing control rather than an empty state.

The set is open, so it is accounted for as a whole here and one member of it, `disabled`, is driven above through `via: "rest"` because it is the fieldset host's whole point.

The role-and-disabled story is where that matters: the sheet's ghost rule once out-specified `:disabled`, so a disabled ghost button kept its switched-on colours for a whole save.

note: The tri-state is the point: `indeterminate` is a DOM PROPERTY with no HTML attribute, so a hand-rolled box that set it in markup set nothing at all, silently. The states story is where a reader confirms that a box which is both checked and indeterminate reads as indeterminate — "some of these", which is what a selection header needs.

states.hover: No prop; see the plinth's pseudo-class readout. The wrapper carries `cursor: pointer` and `is-disabled` swaps it for `not-allowed`.

note: `onChange` declares `writes: "value"`, so pressing the component's OWN plus and minus buttons moves the rendered number and typing in the field commits through the same path. Without it the specimen would log and never move. The primary control is the input, not the adjuncts: a click-only stepper is a documented keyboard regression.
